newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed after early fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed after early fund buying.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with a late break in soybean futures taking the glimmer from an early rally in corn which was related to fund buying, traders said.
"Some of them (funds) have been short a long time and may be getting out, taking profits before the end of the year," a trader said.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report Friday showed funds were short corn by roughly 270.5 million bushels as of December 17 and long about 79.4 million.
The fund demand totaled roughly 12.0 million bushels with Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins each purchasing about five million bushels of the March contract, traders said.
Slow farmer selling also lent support, the traders said.
Corn was pressed by not only the drop in soybeans but by near-ideal crop weather in South America and only routine export sales of U.S. corn, the traders said.
March corn traded in a 4-3/4 cent per bushel range and volume was thin leaving open the potential for volatility.
Corn closed one cent per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with March up 1/4 at $2.67.
Spread trading centered on The Chicago Corp's bear spread of two million bushels of July/March at 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents and bull spread of one million bushels of May/July at one cent, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 32,000 contracts, above the 18,117 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, LFG Futures sold 250 March $2.80 calls at 2-1/2 to 2-3/8 cents and Refco Inc bought 200 March $2.40 puts at 5/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, above the 2,957 traded Tuesday.
